audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for locusts, Pharaoh's servants' protest, partial release bargaining, darkness, and final rupture.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Come to Pharaoh, for I have made his heart heavy and heart of his servants, so that I may set these signs of mine in his midst,

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him:

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them,

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל פַּרְעֹ֑ה כִּֽי אֲנִ֞י הִכְבַּ֤דְתִּי אֶת לִבּוֹ֙ וְאֶת לֵ֣ב עֲבָדָ֔יו לְמַ֗עַן שִׁתִ֛י אֹתֹתַ֥י אֵ֖לֶּה בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: and so that you may recount in ears of your child and your child's child how I dealt with Egypt and my signs that I set among them, and you shall know that I am YHWH.

familiar.text: And that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know how that I am the LORD.

modern.text: and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians when I performed miraculous signs among them, so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.”

original.text: וּלְמַ֡עַן תְּסַפֵּר֩ בְּאָזְנֵ֨י בִנְךָ֜ וּבֶן בִּנְךָ֗ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִתְעַלַּ֨לְתִּי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶת אֹתֹתַ֖י אֲשֶׁר שַׂ֣מְתִּי בָ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and said to him, Thus says YHWH, Divine of Hebrews: Until when will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Send my people away, so they may serve/worship me.

familiar.text: And Moses and Aaron came in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.

modern.text: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and told him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹן֮ אֶל פַּרְעֹה֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים עַד מָתַ֣י מֵאַ֔נְתָּ לֵעָנֹ֖ת מִפָּנָ֑י שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי

verses.restored: For if you refuse to send my people, look, tomorrow I bring locusts into your border.

familiar.text: Else, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to morrow will I bring the locusts into thy coast:

modern.text: But if you refuse to let My people go, I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.

original.text: כִּ֛י אִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ אֶת עַמִּ֑י הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא מָחָ֛ר אַרְבֶּ֖ה בִּגְבֻלֶֽךָ

verses.restored: They will cover eye of land so no one can see the land, and they will eat remnant left to you from hail, and eat every tree sprouting for you from the field.

familiar.text: And they shall cover the face of the earth, that one cannot be able to see the earth: and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which groweth for you out of the field:

modern.text: They will cover the face of the land so that no one can see it. They will devour whatever is left after the hail and eat every tree that grows in your fields.

original.text: וְכִסָּה֙ אֶת עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאָכַ֣ל אֶת יֶ֣תֶר הַפְּלֵטָ֗ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֤רֶת לָכֶם֙ מִן הַבָּרָ֔ד וְאָכַל֙ אֶת כָּל הָעֵ֔ץ הַצֹּמֵ֥חַ לָכֶ֖ם מִן הַשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: They will fill your houses, houses of all your servants, and houses of all Egypt, which your fathers and fathers of your fathers did not see from day they were on ground until this day. He turned and went out from Pharaoh.

familiar.text: And they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; which neither thy fathers, nor thy fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned himself, and went out from Pharaoh.

modern.text: They will fill your houses and the houses of all your officials and every Egyptian—something neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen since the day they came into this land.’” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh’s presence.

original.text: וּמָלְא֨וּ בָתֶּ֜יךָ וּבָתֵּ֣י כָל עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ וּבָתֵּ֣י כָל מִצְרַיִם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא רָא֤וּ אֲבֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ וַאֲב֣וֹת אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ מִיּ֗וֹם הֱיוֹתָם֙ עַל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּ֥פֶן וַיֵּצֵ֖א מֵעִ֥ם פַּרְעֹֽה

verses.restored: Pharaoh's servants said to him, Until when will this one be a snare to us? Send the men, so they may serve/worship YHWH their Divine. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined?

familiar.text: And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the LORD their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?

modern.text: Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is in ruins?”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י פַרְעֹ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו עַד מָתַי֙ יִהְיֶ֨ה זֶ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְיַֽעַבְד֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם הֲטֶ֣רֶם תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י אָבְדָ֖ה מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, Go, serve/worship YHWH your Divine. Who and who are going?

familiar.text: And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve the LORD your God: but who are they that shall go?

modern.text: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the LORD your God,” he said. “But who exactly will be going?”

original.text: וַיּוּשַׁ֞ב אֶת מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽת אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֥וּ עִבְד֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם מִ֥י וָמִ֖י הַהֹלְכִֽים

verses.restored: Moses said, With our young and our old we will go; with our sons and daughters, with our flock and herd we will go, because we have festival to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto the LORD.

modern.text: “We will go with our young and old,” Moses replied. “We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast to the LORD.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה בִּנְעָרֵ֥ינוּ וּבִזְקֵנֵ֖ינוּ נֵלֵ֑ךְ בְּבָנֵ֨ינוּ וּבִבְנוֹתֵ֜נוּ בְּצֹאנֵ֤נוּ וּבִבְקָרֵ֨נוּ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֥י חַג יְהוָ֖ה לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: He said to them, May YHWH be with you if I send you and your little ones. See, harm is before your faces.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Let the LORD be so with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look to it; for evil is before you.

modern.text: Then Pharaoh told them, “May the LORD be with you if I ever let you go with your little ones. Clearly you are bent on evil.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם יְהִ֨י כֵ֤ן יְהוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת טַפְּכֶ֑ם רְא֕וּ כִּ֥י רָעָ֖ה נֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Not so. Go now, the men, and serve/worship YHWH, for that is what you seek. And they were driven out from Pharaoh's face.

familiar.text: Not so: go now ye that are men, and serve the LORD; for that ye did desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

modern.text: No, only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been requesting.” And Moses and Aaron were driven from Pharaoh’s presence.

original.text: לֹ֣א כֵ֗ן לְכֽוּ נָ֤א הַגְּבָרִים֙ וְעִבְד֣וּ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ אַתֶּ֣ם מְבַקְשִׁ֑ים וַיְגָ֣רֶשׁ אֹתָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Stretch your hand over land of Egypt for locusts, and they shall go up over land of Egypt and eat every plant of land, all that hail left.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, so that the locusts may swarm over it and devour every plant in the land—everything that the hail has left behind.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֨ה יָדְךָ֜ עַל אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בָּֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְיַ֖עַל עַל אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְיֹאכַל֙ אֶת כָּל עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁאִ֖יר הַבָּרָֽד

verses.restored: Moses stretched his staff over land of Egypt, and YHWH drove east wind through the land all that day and all night; morning came, and east wind carried the locusts.

familiar.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.

modern.text: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land. By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת מַטֵּהוּ֮ עַל אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיהוָ֗ה נִהַ֤ג ר֥וּחַ קָדִים֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ כָּל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וְכָל הַלָּ֑יְלָה הַבֹּ֣קֶר הָיָ֔ה וְר֨וּחַ֙ הַקָּדִ֔ים נָשָׂ֖א אֶת הָאַרְבֶּֽה

modern.text: The locusts swarmed across the land and settled over the entire territory of Egypt. Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֗ה עַ֚ל כָּל אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיָּ֕נַח בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד לְ֠פָנָיו לֹא הָ֨יָה כֵ֤ן אַרְבֶּה֙ כָּמֹ֔הוּ וְאַחֲרָ֖יו לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה כֵּֽן

verses.restored: They covered eye of all land, and land became dark; they ate every plant of land and all fruit of trees left by hail, and no green thing remained on tree or plant of field in all land of Egypt.

familiar.text: For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left: and there remained not any green thing in the trees, or in the herbs of the field, through all the land of Egypt.

modern.text: They covered the face of all the land until it was black, and they consumed all the plants on the ground and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left behind. Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.

modern.text: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.

verses.restored: Now please lift my sin/misalignment just this once, and plead to YHWH your Divine, that he remove from me only this death.

familiar.text: Now therefore forgive, I pray thee, my sin only this once, and intreat the LORD your God, that he may take away from me this death only.

modern.text: Now please forgive my sin once more and appeal to the LORD your God, that He may remove this death from me.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שָׂ֣א נָ֤א חַטָּאתִי֙ אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֔עַם וְהַעְתִּ֖ירוּ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָסֵר֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י רַ֖ק אֶת הַמָּ֥וֶת הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: He went out from Pharaoh and pleaded to YHWH.

modern.text: So Moses left Pharaoh’s presence and appealed to the LORD.

modern.text: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind that carried off the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained anywhere in Egypt.

original.text: וַיַּהֲפֹ֨ךְ יְהוָ֤ה רֽוּחַ יָם֙ חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֔ד וַיִּשָּׂא֙ אֶת הָ֣אַרְבֶּ֔ה וַיִּתְקָעֵ֖הוּ יָ֣מָּה סּ֑וּף לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ אַרְבֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם

modern.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go. The Ninth Plague: Darkness

familiar.text: And Pharaoh called unto Moses, and said, Go ye, serve the LORD; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed: let your little ones also go with you.

modern.text: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you; only your flocks and herds must stay behind.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְכוּ֙ עִבְד֣וּ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה רַ֛ק צֹאנְכֶ֥ם וּבְקַרְכֶ֖ם יֻצָּ֑ג גַּֽם טַפְּכֶ֖ם יֵלֵ֥ךְ עִמָּכֶֽם

verses.restored: Moses said, You yourself must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, and we will make them for YHWH our Divine.

familiar.text: And Moses said, Thou must give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice unto the LORD our God.

modern.text: But Moses replied, “You must also provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּם אַתָּ֛ה תִּתֵּ֥ן בְּיָדֵ֖נוּ זְבָחִ֣ים וְעֹל֑וֹת וְעָשִׂ֖ינוּ לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: And also our livestock shall go with us; not a hoof shall remain, for from it we must take to serve/worship YHWH our Divine, and we do not know with what we must serve/worship YHWH until we come there.

familiar.text: Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not an hoof be left behind; for thereof must we take to serve the LORD our God; and we know not with what we must serve the LORD, until we come thither.

modern.text: Even our livestock must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for we will need some of them to worship the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to worship the LORD until we arrive.”

original.text: וְגַם מִקְנֵ֜נוּ יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗נוּ לֹ֤א תִשָּׁאֵר֙ פַּרְסָ֔ה כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ נִקַּ֔ח לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ לֹֽא נֵדַ֗ע מַֽה נַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה עַד בֹּאֵ֖נוּ שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: YHWH strengthened/hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was not willing to send them.

familiar.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let them go.

modern.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.

original.text: וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לְשַׁלְּחָֽם

verses.restored: Pharaoh said to him, Go from me. Guard yourself; do not see my face again, for in day you see my face you shall die.

familiar.text: And Pharaoh said unto him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die.

modern.text: “Depart from me!” Pharaoh said to Moses. “Make sure you never see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר ל֥וֹ פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֣ךְ מֵעָלָ֑י הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ אֶל תֹּ֨סֶף֙ רְא֣וֹת פָּנַ֔י כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם רְאֹתְךָ֥ פָנַ֖י תָּמֽוּת

verses.restored: Moses said, As you have spoken: I will not see your face again.

familiar.text: And Moses said, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.

modern.text: “As you say,” Moses replied, “I will never see your face again.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה כֵּ֣ן דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ לֹא אֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד רְא֥וֹת פָּנֶֽיךָ

translation_notes: The signs become intergenerational memory: tell your child and child's child.
Pharaoh's servants now protest Pharaoh's refusal; this again blocks ethnic flattening.
Pharaoh repeatedly bargains for partial liberation: men only, then people without livestock. Moses insists total release for worship-service.
safety_note: Locust and darkness signs should be read within the liberation confrontation. Do not celebrate ecological devastation; note the text's own concern that Egypt is ruined by Pharaoh's refusal.
